notes: Files read: CommonClientConfigs.java, consumer/ConsumerConfig.java, consumer/internals/AbstractCoordinator.java, consumer/internals/ConsumerCoordinator.java, consumer/internals/Heartbeat.java (all under research/ontology/vendor/libs/kafka-clients@3.6.0/clients/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/clients/).
Config keys: the key names are defined in CommonClientConfigs.java (lines 162, 171, 177, 185); ConsumerConfig.java aliases them. The defaults are the define() literals in ConsumerConfig.java.

rebalance.timeout.ms: no default is stated in the vendored files (no define() in ConsumerConfig.java; GroupRebalanceConfig is not vendored), so no config-default fact is reported. Heartbeat.java:49-50 computes the poll timer from config.rebalanceTimeoutMs, and the mapping from max.poll.interval.ms to that field is not in the vendored files.

group.instance.id: default is null (ConsumerConfig.java:372). The schema value types cannot express null, so no config-default fact is reported for it. Static membership (non-null group.instance.id) is covered by the note on the CommonClientConfigs.java:169 fact, and by AbstractCoordinator.java:1127-1128, which says a static member never sends LeaveGroup and its membership expires only by session timeout.

session.timeout.ms: the Heartbeat.java sessionTimer uses config.sessionTimeoutMs (Heartbeat.java:48). The mapping from the session.timeout.ms key to that field is not in the vendored files; the key name is taken from CommonClientConfigs.java:177.

Removal signal: no coordinator-side log, exception or exposed name for removing a member is stated in these five files. The only removal-related text in ConsumerCoordinator.java (lines 347, 370) concerns pause flags. AbstractCoordinator.java:1133-1134 logs the client's own LeaveGroup request, which is not a coordinator removal, so it is not reported as a removal-signal fact.

The broker and group coordinator are not vendored. Facts that name the group-coordinator as the failure detector cite the documentation string in CommonClientConfigs.java and state that as the file's own description of broker behaviour.

facts.subject: retry.backoff.ms

facts.subject: session.timeout.ms
facts.note: The documentation string at CommonClientConfigs.java:178-181 says the broker removes the client when no heartbeat arrives before session.timeout.ms expires. The broker source is not vendored, so this is the file's own description of broker behaviour.

facts.subject: session.timeout.ms
facts.note: Static-member path. For a consumer with non-null group.instance.id that reaches max.poll.interval.ms, the doc at CommonClientConfigs.java:166-169 says it stops sending heartbeats and partitions are reassigned only after session.timeout.ms expires. The doc does not name the component; value is extractor-assigned from the coordinator-side reassignment described there. Broker source not vendored.

facts.subject: max.poll.interval.ms
facts.note: Detected by the client's HeartbeatThread (AbstractCoordinator.java:1398-1487), not the broker. The timer is set from config.rebalanceTimeoutMs (Heartbeat.java:49-50). On expiry it logs a warning (AbstractCoordinator.java:1481) and calls maybeLeaveGroup (AbstractCoordinator.java:1487). The doc at CommonClientConfigs.java:163-166 says the consumer is then considered failed.

facts.subject: session.timeout.ms
facts.note: This is the client's own session timer (Heartbeat.java:48, reset on each received heartbeat at Heartbeat.java:93). It detects that this client's session has lapsed, not another member's failure. On expiry it marks the coordinator unknown (AbstractCoordinator.java:1476-1477) and does not itself remove any member.

facts.subject: HeartbeatThread
facts.note: The HeartbeatThread is a separate KafkaThread, started by heartbeatThread.start() at AbstractCoordinator.java:394-395. The foreground poll path only resets the poll timer (Heartbeat.java:62-65, pollTimer.reset at line 64). The heartbeat thread also runs the poll-timeout check (AbstractCoordinator.java:1478), so a stalled foreground thread is detected from that thread.
